correctness.rationale: The inverse of I-rJ has entries r^(k-i) for k>=i. Embedding R_n/n as step kernels gives Hilbert-Schmidt convergence to Volterra T_s with Robin-Dirichlet spectral roots Phi(w)=s; simplicity orders fixed-rank branches. The exact B_n*B_n tridiagonal eigen-equation sin((n+1)theta)=r sin(n theta) leads, with z=n²theta², to s=Phi(z)sin(sqrt(z)/n)/(sqrt(z)/n)+n[cos(sqrt(z)/n)-1]. Its expansion gives z=w+w/(2Phi'(w)n)+O(n^-2), whence the announced constant (s-1)/[4sqrt(s²+w)Phi'(w)]. Phi'<0 on every branch, including at w=0. The direct positive ground-state identity with y_i=n+1-i proves min eigenvalue n^-2 for r=(n+1)/n and ||R_n||=n exactly. I reproduced that identity in exact Fractions for n=2,3,5,20 and independently computed numerical eigenvalues at s=-2,0,1/2,1,2 and j=1,2,3 to check n-scaled residuals. All-domain proof is analytic; the samples do not prove uniformity.
